Question B-006-005-007.

Why the correct answer is right: When the line impedance and antenna input impedance differ, part of the wave is reflected at the antenna. The forward and reflected waves add along the line, producing standing waves.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "heat is produced at the junction": Mismatch loss is dissipated along real line resistance and dielectric loss, not mainly as heat at the single junction between line and antenna.
- sourceIndex 2: "the SWR reading falls to 1:1": A 1:1 SWR is the matched condition; an impedance mismatch makes the SWR rise, not fall to the ideal value.
- sourceIndex 3: "the antenna will not radiate any signal": Most mismatched antennas still radiate some signal; the mismatch reduces power transfer and creates reflections, but it does not automatically stop all radiation.
